g.text: RoPE — Rotary Position Embedding, with the math and the shapes
Explained on: session 07 RoPE (notebook 07_rope.ipynb, code: src/kv_cache_variants/rope.py) · RoFormer arXiv 2104.09864 · YaRN arXiv 2309.00071 · see also mla.excalidraw (decoupled RoPE)
Running example: one attention head, d_h = 128 → 64 rotation pairs, i = 0 … 63 · base = 10000 (RoFormer, Llama-2) · Llama-3 uses base = 500000 · q, k ∈ R^128 per head per token
1 · Why a position signal at all?
Attention by itself is permutation-equivariant (no notion of order): score(m, n) = q_mᵀ k_n / √d_h
contains no m or n. Shuffle the tokens → the same scores, just shuffled. Order must be injected.
x_m ← x_m + p_m (added at the input)
q_m ← R_m q_m , k_n ← R_n k_n
(multiply, on every layer, Q and K only)
→ depends ONLY on the offset n − m
Key insight: RoPE encodes ABSOLUTE position into q and k (each rotated by its own index), but the
dot product only sees the DIFFERENCE of the two rotations → relative position for free.
Each consecutive PAIR of a q/k vector is a 2-D point; rotate it by angle m·θ_i:
└ x'_2i+1 ┘ └ sin mθ_i cos mθ_i ┘ └ x_2i+1 ┘
θ_i = base^(−2i/d_h) (rad per token, pair i)
Key insight: rotation is orthogonal → it never changes |q| or |k|, only their angle. Position
information lives purely in angles, so content magnitude (what the token 'is') is untouched.
Full head vector q ∈ R^128 → 64 independent 2-D rotations = block-diagonal R_m (128×128):
Five 'clock hands' at the same position m = 10 (angle = 10·θ_i):
Key insight: low i = high frequency = sensitive to small offsets (local syntax); high i = low
frequency = barely moves over thousands of tokens (long-range / 'semantic' channel). One vector
carries a whole bank of clocks running at geometrically spaced speeds.
Same thing in complex numbers (how RoFormer writes it): pair i ↔ one complex number
z_i = x_2i + j·x_2i+1 (64 complex numbers per 128-d vector)
RoPE(z_i, m) = z_i · e^{j·m·θ_i} (rotation = multiply by a unit phasor)
q̃_i = q_i e^{j m θ_i}, k̃_i = k_i e^{j n θ_i}
q̃ᵀk̃ (real dot product) = Re Σ_i q̃_i · conj(k̃_i)
= Re Σ_i q_i conj(k_i) · e^{j (m − n) θ_i}
Code equivalent (torch.polar / view_as_complex in Llama reference code):
Key insight: e^{jmθ}·conj(e^{jnθ}) = e^{j(m−n)θ}. Phases multiply, so the absolute phases cancel —
this one line IS the relative-position property.
Long-term decay (RoFormer §3.4.3): |Σ_i q_i conj(k_i) e^{j(m−n)θ_i}| tends to shrink as |m−n| grows,
because the 64 phasors spin at different speeds and stop adding coherently.
5 · Proof: ⟨R_m q, R_n k⟩ = ⟨q, R_{n−m} k⟩ (relative position)
Step 1 q̃_m = R_m q , k̃_n = R_n k q, k ∈ R^128 ; R_m, R_n ∈ R^(128×128)
Step 2 q̃_mᵀ k̃_n = (R_m q)ᵀ (R_n k) = qᵀ R_mᵀ R_n k
Step 3 R_mᵀ = R_m⁻¹ = R_{−m} (rotation is orthogonal; per 2×2 block)
Step 4 R_{−m} R_n = R_{n−m} (angles add: −mθ_i + nθ_i = (n−m)θ_i)
Step 5 q̃_mᵀ k̃_n = qᵀ R_{n−m} k ⇒ ⟨R_m q, R_n k⟩ = ⟨q, R_{n−m} k⟩ □
Worked numbers (pair i = 0, θ₀ = 1 rad/token, q = k = (1, 0)):
query at m = 2, key at n = 5 → angles 2 rad, 5 rad → score = cos(5 − 2) = cos 3 = −0.990
query at m = 10, key at n = 13 → angles 10 rad, 13 rad → score = cos(13 − 10) = cos 3 = −0.990 (identical)
blue = q, red = k : same relative angle

Key insight: the cached key never needs to know where the query will be. Any (m, n) with the same n − m gives the same score — exactly the translation-invariance language needs ('the word 3 tokens ago').
λ_i (tokens per full turn), log scale
Key insight: wavelengths form a geometric series from 6.3 tokens to 54K (or 2.6M) tokens.
Raising the base (Llama-3: 500000) slows the slow pairs → more pairs can still tell far
Problem: pairs whose λ_i exceeds the training length (right of the red line crossing)
never completed one full turn during training. Past L_train they produce angles the
model has never seen → this is where length extrapolation breaks (section 9).
# rope.py — build once, shapes for d_h = 128
x1, x2 = x.chunk(2, -1) # (B, H, T, 64) each
element j+64 : q'_{j+64} = q_{j+64}·cos(mθ_j) + q_j·sin(mθ_j) ← the 2×2 rotation
Trade-off / gotcha: HF & this repo pair dims (j, j+64) ('half-split'); the paper and Meta's complex
code pair (2i, 2i+1) ('interleaved'). Same math up to a fixed permutation of W_q/W_k rows — but the
checkpoint and kernel MUST agree (HF conversion scripts permute W_q, W_k for this reason).
8 · Q & K only, and how RoPE meets the KV cache
RoPE touches Q and K only — never V, never the residual stream:
Decode step t with a KV cache (shapes: Llama-3-8B, H_q=32, H_kv=8, d_h=128):
K-cache (B, 8, t, 128): keys stored ALREADY rotated at their absolute position n
score(t, n) = (R_t q_t)ᵀ(R_n k_n)/√128 = q_tᵀ R_{n−t} k_n /√128
work per step: rotate 1 q (32×128) + 1 k (8×128) → O(H·d_h)
old keys are never re-rotated: their n is fixed; only q moves
Key insight: because relative position emerges from the dot product, RoPE is cache-friendly —
rotate once at write time, append, done (notebook 07 checks: rotating at offset = past_len
Problem: absolute positions are baked into the cached K. Anything that renumbers positions
(sliding window / attention-sink re-indexing, changing θ for context extension, MLA weight
absorption) needs pre-RoPE K or a re-rotation R_Δ — and RoPE is why MLA needs a decoupled
path (W^UQ_iᵀ R_{n−t} W^UK_i is position-dependent, see docs/MLA.excalidraw).
9 · Context extension: beyond the trained length
Failure mode: train at L_train (e.g. 8192), run at L' = s·L_train. Fast pairs have seen every angle many times; slow pairs (λ_i > L_train) only saw an arc → unseen angles,
attention logits out of distribution, perplexity explodes just past L_train. Fixes rescale θ_i (example: L_train = 8192, base 10000, d_h = 128, s = 4):
multiplier on θ_i per pair (1 = untouched, 1/4 = ÷ s), i = 0 … 60 step 4
Key insight: don't squash the fast pairs (they encode local order, already seen at every angle);
only stretch the slow pairs that never completed a turn. NTK does it smoothly via the base,
YaRN does it explicitly per pair — Llama-3's base 500000 bakes a slower spectrum in from the start.
Trade-off: every rescaling changes θ_i, so (a) the model usually needs a short long-context
fine-tune, and (b) a KV cache written under one θ is invalid under another (dynamic schemes).
Longer context also means a linearly bigger KV cache: 2·L·B·T·H_kv·d_h·S.
q̃_m = R_m q, k̃_n = R_n k ⟨R_m q, R_n k⟩ = ⟨q, R_{n−m} k⟩
code: x*cos + rotate_half(x)*sin on Q (B,H_q,T,128) and K (B,H_kv,T,128), not V
cache: store rotated K at absolute n; rotate only the new q, k at step t
extend: PI m/s · NTK base·s^(d/(d−2)) · YaRN per-pair ramp + 0.1·ln s + 1 temperature
